questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Endianness is a practical concern in systems and networking. This question tests precise bit-twiddling with masks and shifts, without relying on loops. It also checks understanding of how a 32-bit word maps to byte positions.

## Key Concepts
- Byte extraction with masks
- Shifting to relocate bytes
- Endianness awareness and portability
- No loops; pure bitwise operations

## Code Example
```c
uint32_t swapEndian32(uint32_t n) {
  return (n >> 24) | ((n >> 8) & 0x0000FF00) | ((n << 8) & 0x00FF0000) | (n << 24);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you generalize to 64-bit values?
- How would you implement an endianness swap for 16-bit values or for an array of 32-bit words efficiently?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement a fixed-width rotate using only bit ops and to reason about edge-case n=0. 

## Key Concepts
- Fixed-width rotation formula; wrap-around behavior.
- Safe shift amounts via masking to handle n=0.
- No loops or conditionals in a single expression.

## Code Example
```javascript
uint128 rotateLeft128(uint128 x, uint128 n) {
  return (x << n) | (x >> ((128 - n) & 127));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you generalize to rotateRight128? 
- What are potential portability concerns across compilers for uint128?

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to reason about 128-bit bit patterns and leverage existing helper functions to implement non-trivial properties without using conditional branches.

## Key Concepts
- Bit reversal and palindrome detection in 128-bit space
- Constant-time, branchless implementation
- Integration with existing `reverse128` utility

## Code Example
```c
int isPalindrome128(uint64_t hi, uint64_t lo) {
  uint64_t rhi, rlo;
  reverse128(hi, lo, &rhi, &rlo);
  return (rhi == hi && rlo == lo);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this approach to 256-bit values?
- What optimizations could be applied if the function were called frequently?
